title: Revealing Many-Body Phases at finite temperatures through Quantum Coherence Distribution
authors: Antonio Palamara, Nicola Lo Gullo, Antonello Sindona, Francesco Plastina
abstract: We introduce a diagnostic framework based on the full probability distribution of quantum coherence to probe single-particle and many-body phases at finite temperature. We first apply this approach to the localization transition in the non-interacting Aubry-André model and then extend the analysis to its interacting counterpart, whose phase diagram is substantially richer. We show that the moments of the coherence distribution provide clear signatures of quantum phase transitions and capture the emergence of many-body phases. More importantly, we find that the entropy of the coherence distribution emerges as an even more powerful indicator, retaining clear signatures of the underlying quantum phases while remaining remarkably robust against increasing thermal fluctuations.
summary: This work introduces a novel diagnostic tool based on the entropy of the quantum coherence distribution to characterize quantum phases. By applying it to the interacting Aubry-André model, the authors demonstrate that this entropy remains robustly sensitive to quantum phase transitions, even when significant thermal fluctuations are present, outperforming simpler moment-based diagnostics.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a diagnostic framework to probe both single-particle and many-body quantum phases at finite temperatures, where thermal fluctuations typically obscure quantum critical signatures.
main_result: The entropy of the quantum coherence distribution ($H_c$) proves to be a significantly more robust indicator than individual moments, retaining clear signatures of underlying quantum phases across increasing thermal fluctuations.
method: The authors construct a diagnostic based on the full probability distribution of quantum coherence, derived via a Two-Point Measurement protocol, and analyze its statistical moments, particularly its entropy.
model_or_system: The analysis is first applied to the non-interacting Aubry-André (AA) model to study localization transitions, and then extended to the interacting AA model containing spinless fermions with nearest-neighbor interactions.
key_observables: Entropy of the coherence distribution ($H_c$), first and higher-order moments of the coherence distribution, and the relative entropy of coherence ($C[\hat{ho}]$).
important_parameters: Finite temperature ($ eta$), potential strength ($V_0$), and interaction strength ($U$). The localization transition is marked by $V_0=2$ in the non-interacting case.
main_assumptions: The analysis of the interacting model is computationally limited to small system sizes ($N=12$) due to the exponential growth of the Hilbert space.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the finite-temperature behavior of coherence moments and entropy for the non-interacting model, and compare ground-state versus thermal-state coherence and entropy across the phase diagram of the interacting model.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the diagnostic framework using the non-interacting AA model to show $H_c$'s robustness against temperature. It then extends this analysis to the interacting AA model to characterize three distinct many-body phases (Metallic, ABI, CDW) using $H_c$ as the primary tool.
why_interesting: The focus on using coherence entropy to distinguish quantum phases from thermal noise is highly relevant for AMO physics, as many experimental platforms (like cold atoms) are inherently studied at finite, non-zero temperatures.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
